functional_impact_measured: Tag used for both detection (surface expression) and ACE2 enzymatic activity assays; the paper reports the construct is functional in activity assays, indicating enzymatic activity is preserved with the N-terminal tag.
rationale: L2 explicitly states the tag is 'N-terminally fused' to ACE2 constructs. ACE2 is a type-I single-pass TM protein with its N-terminus extracellular (signal peptide 1-17, mature N-terminus at Q18). A tag N-terminally fused to the full-length protein must be placed after the signal peptide cleavage site to avoid being cleaved off; the junction is therefore after residue 17 (A17|Q18), computed from the SP landmark. The extracellular domain spans residues 18-743 (726 aa), placing this site 726 residues from the TM boundary with no steric concern. The construct was used in both detection and activity assays, confirming surface expression and preserved enzymatic function. Full-length ACE2 constructs (including chimeras) expressed in mammalian cells with a 4xmyc tag and/or human placenta alkaline phosphatase (AP) tag N-terminally fused, used for detection and enzymatic activity assays (PMC13342293). The paper explicitly states 'N-terminally fused'; no residue number is given. The signal peptide spans residues 1-17 (landmark-derived); the mature N-terminus begins at Q18. An N-terminal fusion on a type-I TM protein with an extracellular N-terminus places the tag on the extracellular face after SP cleavage, so the junction is insert_after_residue=17 (A17|Q18), derived from the SP landmark.

rationale: Human ACHE has a signal peptide spanning residues 1–31 (authoritative landmark); the mature N-terminus begins at residue 32 (E). A tag placed after residue 31 is therefore on the extracellular face, well clear of any TM boundary (the protein is GPI-anchored with no TM helix). Python verification confirms residue 31 = A and residue 32 = E in the canonical sequence. No specific residue number is cited in L1 or L3/L4; the position is topology-derived from the single free extracellular terminus of the mature protein. L1 (BmAChE) and L3/L4 (DmAChE) are both indirect evidence (insect orthologs), but both independently place a FLAG tag at the N-terminus of the full-length, membrane-anchored AChE, mapping to the same junction in human ACHE. BmAChE (Bombyx mori AChE, ortholog of human ACHE) was expressed as a full-length fusion with an α-agglutinin (AGα1) membrane anchor in P. pastoris, with a FLAG tag placed at the N-terminus of the AChE coding sequence. The construct is membrane-anchored and surface-displayed; the FLAG is on the extracellular face. UAA incorporated at position 534 via PylRS-AF/tRNA-Pyl system, then labeled with ATTO488-tz by click chemistry in living neurons. Note: human NFASC position 534 is R (arginine), not K; rat has K534 at this position — species difference at this single residue.
